note: THE VECTOR SET of the registration kind's six bodies -- the request's two kinds, fresh and board-carries-on, the three answers, approved, refused and denied, and the vouch (REG-1.86; the canonical rule) -- in the one scheme of records.json, the binding's and the endpoint's set beside this one: every parser of the bodies runs these in its own gate. The rule is the arbiter: parse(b) answers a record only where b == encode(parse(b)). `kind` is the kind the caller names, the link's type slot, spelled as its row's type string; `parse` is the parse's answer, `ok` (admitted: the bytes ARE the canonical form) or the refusal's cause as skep-registry's ParseRefusal::token spells it, which the daemon joins to its malformed_record token; on an admitted body `canonical_sigless` is the sig-less canonical projection a record-grade signature ranges over and `sig` the sig member as found (null where absent). A body carried as `bytes_hex` is bytes that are no UTF-8 string. A body carried as `bytes_filled` is its `head`, then its `fill` repeated, then its `tail`, the fill's run as long as makes the whole body `len` bytes -- the cap's vectors, whose bytes are long and all one character; where such a body is admitted its sig member is that run, `sig_filled`. The cap is per kind, `caps`, with the sig member inside it, counted in the body's UTF-8 bytes: 64 KiB for a request of either kind and 16 KiB for every other body, each a term of the format (REG-1.86 (h)). The parse checks each member's FORM and never its admissibility: a `why` says where a body that parses is refused by a later reader -- the board at its registry sequence, or a console.
